cards.text: James is writing to believers he calls "my brothers." He just finished saying faith without deeds is dead. Now he's got a warning for everybody who wants to stand up front and teach.

cards.question: James says not many of his brothers should become teachers. Why?

answers.text: Teachers will be judged more strictly
Teachers will be paid too little

cards.text: Then James gets right in line with everybody: we all stumble in many ways. Friend, I once stamped FORTY cookies upside down and told the oven it was a new style.

cards.question: James says if anyone is never at fault in what he says, he is a perfect man, able to control his whole ___.

cards.text: Then James grabs a picture everybody knows: a big horse with a little bit in its mouth. That whole animal, and a tiny piece of gear is running the show.

cards.question: When people put bits into horses' mouths to make them obey, what can they do?
Next James points to ships. They're huge, and strong winds drive them. What steers a ship wherever the pilot wants?
After the bit and the rudder, James turns to the tongue. True or false: he calls the tongue the strongest part of the body.
James says the tongue is small but boasts of great things. Then he names another small thing with a huge result. What does he say a small spark can do?

cards.text: And James doesn't soften it one bit. The tongue is a fire, a world of wickedness among the parts of the body, and it is itself set on fire by hell.

cards.question: James says the fire of the tongue ___ the whole person and sets the course of his life on fire.

cards.text: Then James runs down the list: animals, birds, reptiles and sea creatures, all being tamed by people. Somebody out there tamed a REPTILE, friend, and I still can't get my oven timer to listen to me.

cards.question: True or false: James says people can tame the tongue the same way they tame animals.
James calls the tongue a restless evil, full of deadly ___.

cards.text: Now James gets personal: with the tongue we bless our Lord and Father. Same tongue, same mouth, and then it turns right around and does something else.

cards.question: What else does James say we do with that same tongue we use to bless our Lord and Father?

answers.text: Curse people made in God's likeness
Teach people to fear the Lord

cards.question: Blessing and cursing come out of the same mouth. True or false: James says that's fine as long as there's more blessing than cursing.

cards.text: James wraps up with questions straight out of nature, starting with this one: "Can both fresh water and salt water flow from the same spring?" Picture taking a big drink and getting a mouthful of OCEAN.

cards.question: James keeps going with trees and vines. True or false: he says a fig tree can grow olives.
James asks about the spring, the fig tree and the grapevine. What's he showing about blessing and cursing coming from the same mouth?

findings.problem: The card states a fact from outside the passage, that James just finished saying faith without deeds is dead (James 2:26), but gives no reference for it. The card cites only James 3:1.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: James appears here for the first time with no simple line saying who he is, such as what he calls himself in James 1:1.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to finish James's line ('able to control his whole ___'). Nothing earlier has brought up the body, so the baker is guessing wording, not reasoning out meaning.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The story card says 'That whole animal, and a tiny piece of gear is running the show.' This gives away the answer to card 6 ('Guide the whole animal').

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to finish the line 'full of deadly ___'. It tests the BSB wording ('poison' vs 'smoke' or 'thorns'), not meaning the baker can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Card 15 sets up that the same tongue 'turns right around and does something else' after blessing the Lord. That signals the opposite of blessing. Both wrong answers ('Teach people to fear the Lord', 'Comfort people who are grieving') are good things, so the setup rules them out and the right answer stands out.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.
